name: Beverly Washington

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Merlot, Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sémillon and Cabernet Franc fully without cooking off their freshness.
Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Syrah sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Chardonnay is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Summers are close to rainless. Vines need irrigation or deep soil that stores winter rain, but disease is rare.

soil.rock: Sand is warm and airy. It drains fast but holds little water, and phylloxera does not thrive in it. Loess is fine, wind-blown silt. Fertile and warm, it holds water well but drains poorly.
soil.top: The topsoil drains well and still stores water for dry spells, so vines grow evenly. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Good for generous crops of standard to good wine.
